promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 3 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Welcome back, and glad your mum is home. We will ease into running this week, then build again, and I want to be honest with you about what race day can look like three weeks out.

flags.title: Two weeks off
flags.detail: three planned sessions were missed while your mum was in hospital, so this week restarts gently rather than picking up where we left off.

flags.title: Sleep is low
flags.detail: 6 hours average with high stress makes everything feel harder, so effort may spike on familiar sessions.

flags.title: Race goal needs a rethink
flags.detail: longest run so far is 2.78 km walk-run, and the race is Nov 15, so finishing strong matters more than running every step.

flags.title: Stiffness from driving
flags.detail: watch the first 5 minutes of each run and keep it to a very easy jog until the legs free up.

answers.question: I haven't run for two weeks. Do I have to start again from the beginning? And is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?
answers.answer:
No, you do not start again from the beginning. Two weeks off at this stage costs a little sharpness, not your base, and the walk-run blocks you did in September are still in your legs. We pick up one notch below where we left off, then build for two weeks.

On the 5K: finishing is realistic, and finishing mostly running is realistic. Running every single step of 5 km on Nov 15, without a walk break, is a stretch given your longest effort so far is under 3 km and we have three weeks left. I would rather you cross the line strong with one or two short walk breaks than blow up at 3 km chasing a no-walking rule. If the next two weeks go well we can push the continuous-running blocks right up, and on the day you run by feel.

new.analysis:
## Why this week looks like this

The job this week is to get three runs done without soreness, not to make up lost ground. Jumping straight to longer run intervals after two weeks off is how people tweak a calf, and we cannot afford that with the race close.

Monday steps back one notch to 7 x 2 min run / 1 min walk, which is where you were comfortably running in late September. Wednesday returns to the 8 x 2 min block you had been doing, and Saturday stretches the run interval to 3 minutes so we start pushing the continuous running up. If Saturday feels good, next week we go to 4 and 5 minute run blocks, which is how we build toward running most of the 5K.

## About the race plan

Three weeks out is peak territory, but your peak looks different from a seasoned runner's: we are still extending how long you can run without walking, not sharpening speed. Keep the easy days genuinely easy, treat the rest days as real rest, and let sleep catch up if it can. If a session feels much harder than it should, cut it short rather than grind through, and tell me in your next check-in.
